sentences.zh: 朱宣

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan

sentences.zh: （弟瑾）〉

translations.literal: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉

sentences.zh: 朱宣，宋州下邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從其父販鹽為盜，父抵法死，宣乃去事青州節度使王敬武為軍校，敬武以隸其將曹全晟。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father peddling salt and turned bandit; his father died by law, and Xuan then left to serve Wang Jingwu, military governor of Qingzhou, as a camp officer—Jingwu placed him under his general Cao Quansheng.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he hawked salt with his father and drifted into banditry. When his father was executed, Xuan entered the service of Wang Jingwu, governor of Qingzhou, as a camp officer. Jingwu assigned him to his general Cao Quansheng.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，敬武遣全晟入關與破黃巢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, Jingwu sent Quansheng into the passes to join in breaking Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe 2 (882) Jingwu sent Quansheng through the passes to help crush Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 還過鄆州，鄆州節度使薛崇卒，其將崔君預自稱留後。

translations.literal: On the return they passed Yun prefecture; Yun’s military governor Xue Chong died, and his officer Cui Junyu styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home they passed Yunzhou. The governor Xue Chong had died; his officer Cui Junyu declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 全晟攻殺君預，遂據鄆州。

translations.literal: Quansheng attacked and killed Junyu, then seized Yun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Quansheng struck, killed Junyu, and took Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣以戰功，為鄆州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: For battle merit Xuan was made commander of Yun’s horse-and-foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: For his fighting Xuan was made commander of all horse and foot at Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而全晟死，軍中推宣為留後，唐僖宗即拜宣天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Quansheng died; the army pushed Xuan as acting governor, and Emperor Xizong of Tang at once appointed him military governor of the Tianping circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Quansheng died soon after. The troops made Xuan acting governor, and Tang’s Emperor Xizong named him military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，以兄事宣。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu held Xuanyi and treated Xuan as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen, holding Xuanyi, treated Xuan like an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 太祖新就鎮，兵力尚少，數為秦宗權所困，太祖乞兵於宣。

translations.literal: The Founder had only lately taken his command and his forces were still few; he was repeatedly trapped by Qin Zongquan and begged troops from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen had only just secured his post; his army was still thin, and Qin Zongquan kept pinning him down. He begged Xuan for men.

sentences.zh: 宣與其弟瑾以兗、鄆之兵救汴，大破蔡兵，走宗權。

translations.literal: Xuan and his younger brother Jin brought Yanzhou and Yunzhou troops to rescue Bian, routed the Cai army utterly, and drove Zongquan off.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his brother Jin marched from Yanzhou and Yunzhou to relieve Bian, shattered the Cai host, and drove Zongquan away.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖已襲取滑州，稍欲並吞諸鎮，宣、瑾既還，乃馳檄兗、鄆，言宣、瑾多誘宣武軍卒亡以東，乃發兵收亡卒，因攻之，遂為敵國，苦戰曹、濮間。

translations.literal: By then the Founder had already seized Hua prefecture and little by little meant to swallow the other circuits. When Xuan and Jin returned, he raced proclamations to Yanzhou and Yunzhou, saying Xuan and Jin had lured many Xuanyi soldiers to desert eastward; he then sent troops to round up the deserters and attacked them—thereupon they became enemy states and fought bitterly between Cao and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhu Wen had taken Huazhou and was swallowing rival domains one by one. When Xuan and Jin went home, he fired proclamations at Yanzhou and Yunzhou accusing them of luring Xuanyi troops east. He sent men to hunt deserters, then attacked—brothers became enemies, and the war between Cao and Pu turned savage.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁又東攻徐州，西有蔡賊，北敵強晉，宣、瑾兄弟自相首尾，然卒為梁所滅。

translations.literal: At that time Liang was also attacking Xuzhou in the east, had Cai bandits in the west, and faced powerful Jin in the north; Xuan and Jin, brothers, covered each other’s rear—yet in the end they were destroyed by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was striking Xuzhou in the east, fighting Cai in the west, and facing powerful Jin in the north. The brothers Xuan and Jin shielded each other—yet Liang destroyed them in the end.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年，宣敗，走中都，為葛從周所執，斬於汴橋下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning, Xuan was defeated, fled to Zhongdu, was seized by Ge Congzhou, and beheaded below Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 4 (897) Xuan broke, fled to Zhongdu, was taken by Ge Congzhou, and beheaded beneath Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 瑾，宣從父弟也。

translations.literal: Jin was Xuan’s younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was Xuan’s cousin.

sentences.zh: 從宣居鄆州，補軍校。

translations.literal: He followed Xuan to live at Yun prefecture and was made a camp officer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xuan to Yunzhou and served as a camp officer.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，有大志，兗州節度使齊克讓愛其為人，以女妻之。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and free, with great ambition; Yanzhou’s military governor Qi Kerang loved his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was bold and high-spirited. Qi Kerang, governor of Yanzhou, admired him and gave him his daughter.

sentences.zh: 瑾行親迎，乃選壯士為輿夫，伏兵器輿中。

translations.literal: When Jin went to conduct the wedding in person, he chose stalwart men as sedan-bearers and hid weapons in the sedan.
translations.idiomatic: For the wedding procession Jin chose strong men as litter-bearers and hid weapons inside the bridal sedan.

sentences.zh: 夜至兗州，兵發，遂虜克讓，自稱留後。

translations.literal: At night he reached Yanzhou; the men sprang forth, seized Kerang, and Jin styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Yanzhou by night. The men leaped out, seized Kerang, and Jin declared himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗即拜瑾泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong at once appointed Jin military governor of the Taining circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong immediately named him military governor of Taining.

sentences.zh: 瑾與宣已破秦宗權於汴州，梁太祖責瑾誘宣武軍卒以歸，遣朱珍攻瑾，取曹州，又攻濮州，而太祖自攻鄆。

translations.literal: After Jin and Xuan had broken Qin Zongquan at Bian, Liang Taizu blamed Jin for enticing Xuanyi soldiers to return home, sent Zhu Zhen to attack Jin and take Cao prefecture, then attacked Pu—and the Founder himself attacked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin and Xuan had routed Qin Zongquan at Bian, Zhu Wen accused Jin of luring Xuanyi troops away, sent Zhu Zhen against him, took Caozhou, then Pu—and marched on Yan himself.

sentences.zh: 瑾兄弟往來相救，凡十餘年，大小數十戰，與太祖屢相勝敗。

translations.literal: The brothers rushed to each other’s aid; for more than ten years they fought dozens of battles, large and small, and with the Founder they repeatedly traded victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers raced to rescue each other. For more than ten years they fought dozens of battles with Zhu Wen, winning and losing by turns.

sentences.zh: 太祖得宣將賀瑰、何懷寶及瑾兄瓊，乃將瓊等至兗城下，告瑾曰：「汝兄敗矣！

translations.literal: The Founder captured Xuan’s generals He Gui and He Huaibao and Jin’s elder brother Qiong; he then brought Qiong and the others beneath the walls of Yan and called to Jin: “Your elder brother is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen took Xuan’s generals He Gui and He Huaibao and Jin’s brother Qiong, marched them to the walls of Yanzhou, and shouted: “Your brother is finished!

sentences.zh: 今瓊等已降，不如早自歸。

translations.literal: Now Qiong and the rest have surrendered—you had better yield early.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong and the rest have already surrendered. Yield while you can.

sentences.zh: 」瑾偽曰：「諾。

translations.literal: ” Jin falsely said: “Agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jin lied: “Done.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣牙將胡規持書幣詣軍門請降。

translations.literal: ” He then sent his yamen officer Hu Gui with letters and gifts to the gate to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent his yamen officer Hu Gui to the camp with letters and gifts to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，至延壽門與瑾交語，瑾曰：「願得瓊送符印。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased, came to the Yanshou Gate to speak with Jin face to face; Jin said: “I wish Qiong sent to deliver the tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen was delighted. At the Yanshou Gate he parleyed with Jin, who said: “Send Qiong here with the tally and seal.

sentences.zh: 」太祖信之，遣客將劉捍送瓊往。

translations.literal: ” The Founder believed him and sent his guest officer Liu Han to escort Qiong thither.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhu Wen believed him and sent his guest officer Liu Han to bring Qiong in.

sentences.zh: 瑾伏壯士橋下，單騎迎瓊，揮手語捍曰：「請瓊獨來！

translations.literal: Jin hid stalwarts beneath the bridge, met Qiong alone on horseback, waved his hand and said to Han: “Let Qiong come alone!
translations.idiomatic: Jin hid men under the bridge, rode out alone to meet Qiong, and called to Han: “Send Qiong forward alone!

sentences.zh: 」瓊前，壯士擒之，遂閉門，責瓊先降，斬之，擲其首城外。

translations.literal: ” Qiong advanced; the stalwarts seized him, the gates were shut, Jin rebuked Qiong for surrendering first, beheaded him, and flung his head outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: ” Qiong came forward. The ambush seized him. The gates slammed shut. Jin accused him of yielding first, cut off his head, and threw it over the wall.

sentences.zh: 太祖度不可下，乃留兵圍之而去。

translations.literal: The Founder judged the city could not be taken and left troops to besiege it and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen saw the city would not fall, left an army to besiege it, and marched away.

sentences.zh: 瑾嬰城自守，而與葛從周等戰城下，瑾兵屢敗，宣亦敗於鄆州，乃乞兵於晉，晉遣李承嗣、史儼等以騎兵五千救之。

translations.literal: Jin held the city in defense and fought Ge Congzhou and others beneath the walls; Jin’s troops were repeatedly defeated, Xuan also was defeated at Yun, and he begged troops from Jin; Jin sent Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others with five thousand cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin held the walls and fought Ge Congzhou below them, but his men kept breaking. Xuan lost at Yunzhou and begged Jin for help. Jin sent Li Chengsi and Shi Yan with five thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 太祖已破宣，乃急趨兗。

translations.literal: The Founder had already broken Xuan and then rushed toward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen had already crushed Xuan and now raced on Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾城中食盡，與承嗣等掠食豐、沛間，梁兵奄至，瑾將康懷英等以城降梁。

translations.literal: Food in Jin’s city was exhausted; he and Chengsi and the others foraged between Feng and Pei; Liang troops suddenly arrived, and Jin’s generals Kang Huaiying and others surrendered the city to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou ran out of grain. Jin and Chengsi raided for food between Feng and Pei. Liang troops swept in. Kang Huaiying and other officers handed the city to Liang.

sentences.zh: 瑾等將麾下兵走沂州，沂州刺史尹處賓不納。

translations.literal: Jin and the others led their troops and fled to Yizhou; Yizhou’s prefect Yin Chubin would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fled with his men toward Yizhou. The prefect Yin Chubin refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 又走海州，梁兵急追之，乃奔於淮南。

translations.literal: They fled again to Haizhou; Liang troops pressed close in pursuit, and they ran to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: They ran for Haizhou; Liang gave chase; they crossed into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 楊行密聞瑾來，大喜，解其玉帶贈之，表瑾領武寧軍節度使，以為行軍副使。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi heard Jin had come and was greatly pleased; he unfastened his jade belt and gave it to him, memorialized that Jin should hold the military governorship of Wuning, and made him his deputy in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi rejoiced at Jin’s arrival, gave him his own jade belt, had him named military governor of Wuning, and kept him as field deputy.

sentences.zh: 其後，梁遣龐師古、葛從周等攻淮南，行密用瑾，大破梁兵於清口，斬師古。

translations.literal: Later Liang sent Pang Shigu, Ge Congzhou, and others to attack Huainan; Xingmi used Jin and at Qingkou utterly routed Liang’s army and beheaded Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang sent Pang Shigu and Ge Congzhou against Huainan. Xingmi put Jin in the line. At Qingkou they shattered Liang’s army and killed Shigu.

sentences.zh: 行密累表瑾東南諸道行營副都統、領平盧軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Xingmi repeatedly memorialized Jin as deputy supreme commander of the southeastern circuits’ field headquarters, military governor of Pinglu, and Grand Councilor of the same rank as the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi repeatedly had Jin named deputy supreme commander of the southeastern field armies, governor of Pinglu, and Grand Councilor equal to the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 行密死，渥及隆演相繼立，皆年少，徐溫與其子知訓專政，畏瑾，欲除之，瑾乃謀殺知訓。

translations.literal: When Xingmi died, Wo and Longyan succeeded one after another, both young; Xu Wen and his son Zhixun held power alone, feared Jin, and wished to remove him—Jin then plotted to kill Zhixun.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingmi died, Wo and Longyan were boys in turn on the throne. Xu Wen and his son Zhixun ran everything, feared Jin, and wanted him gone. Jin plotted Zhixun’s death.

sentences.zh: 嘗以月旦遣愛妾候知訓家，知訓強通之，妾歸自訴，瑾益不平。

translations.literal: On the first of the month he once sent a favorite concubine to call on Zhixun’s house; Zhixun forced her and sent her back complaining—Jin grew all the more bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Each month’s first day he sent a favorite concubine to Zhixun’s house. Zhixun took her by force. She came home in tears. Jin’s rage deepened.

sentences.zh: 屢勸隆演誅徐氏，以去國患，隆演不能為。

translations.literal: He repeatedly urged Longyan to execute the Xu clan and remove the state’s peril, but Longyan could not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he pressed Longyan to kill the Xu clan and lift the peril on the state. Longyan would not act.

sentences.zh: 既而知訓以泗州建靜淮軍，出瑾為節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Zhixun established the Jinghuai army at Sizhou and sent Jin out as its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun then founded the Jinghuai army at Sizhou and posted Jin out as its governor.

sentences.zh: 將行，召之夜飲。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he summoned him to drink at night.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure he called Jin to a night’s drinking.

sentences.zh: 明日，知訓過瑾謝，延之升堂，出其妻陶氏，知訓方拜，瑾以笏擊踣之，伏兵自戶突出，殺之。

translations.literal: The next day Zhixun came to Jin’s house to thank him; Jin invited him up to the hall, brought out his wife Lady Tao, and as Zhixun was bowing Jin struck him down with his tablet; hidden troops burst from the doors and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Zhixun came to thank him. Jin drew him into the hall, brought out his wife Lady Tao, and as Zhixun bowed smashed him with his court tablet. Men hidden in the doorways rushed out and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，瑾以二惡馬擊庭中，知訓入而釋馬，使相踶嗚，故外人莫聞其變。

translations.literal: Earlier Jin had set two vicious horses fighting in the courtyard; when Zhixun entered he loosed the horses and let them kick and neigh at each other, so outsiders heard nothing of the change.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had set two savage horses fighting in the courtyard. When Zhixun entered he loosed them to kick and scream, so no one outside heard the killing.

sentences.zh: 瑾攜其首馳示隆演曰：「今日為吳除患矣！

translations.literal: Jin carried the head on horseback to show Longyan and said: “Today I have removed Wu’s scourge!
translations.idiomatic: Jin rode to Longyan with the head in his hand and cried: “Today I have rid Wu of its plague!

sentences.zh: 」隆演曰：「此事非吾敢知！

translations.literal: ” Longyan said: “This affair is not something I dare know of!
translations.idiomatic: ” Longyan said: “This is not mine to know!

sentences.zh: 」遽起入內。

translations.literal: ” He at once rose and went inside.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rose at once and fled inside.

sentences.zh: 瑾忿然以首擊柱，提劍而出，府門已闔，因逾垣，折其足。

translations.literal: Jin in anger struck the pillar with the head, seized his sword and went out—the yamen gates were already shut, so he climbed the wall and broke his foot.
translations.idiomatic: Jin smashed the head against a pillar, drew his sword, and rushed out. The gates were shut. He scaled the wall and broke his foot.

sentences.zh: 瑾顧路窮，大呼曰：「吾為萬人去害，而以一身死之！

translations.literal: Jin, seeing the road at an end, shouted loudly: “I removed a scourge for ten thousand men and die alone for it!
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, he shouted: “I killed the tyrant for the people—and I alone pay with my life!

sentences.zh: 」遂自刎。

translations.literal: ” He then cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 潤州徐知誥聞亂，以兵趨廣陵，族瑾家。

translations.literal: Runzhou’s Xu Zhigao heard of the turmoil and marched troops to Guangling and exterminated Jin’s clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao at Runzhou heard the alarm, marched on Guangling, and wiped out Jin’s house.

sentences.zh: 瑾妻陶氏臨刑而泣，其妾曰：「何為泣乎？

translations.literal: Jin’s wife Lady Tao wept facing execution; a concubine said: “Why weep?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tao wept on the block. A concubine said: “Why cry?

sentences.zh: 今行見公矣！

translations.literal: Soon you will see my lord!
translations.idiomatic: You will see your husband soon enough!

sentences.zh: 」陶氏收淚，欣然就戮，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: ” Lady Tao wiped her tears and went gladly to the blade; those who heard it mourned her.
translations.idiomatic: ” She dried her tears and went to the blade smiling. All who heard it grieved for her.

sentences.zh: 瑾名重江淮，人畏之。

translations.literal: Jin’s name weighed heavy on the Jiang-Huai; men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s name cast a long shadow on the Jiang-Huai. Men feared him.

sentences.zh: 其死也，屍之廣陵北門，路人私共瘞之。

translations.literal: At his death his corpse lay at Guangling’s north gate; passersby privately buried him together.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his body lay at Guangling’s north gate. Travelers buried him in secret.

sentences.zh: 是時，民多病瘧，皆取其墓上土，以水服之，雲病輒愈，更益新土，漸成高墳。

translations.literal: At that time the people often suffered malaria; all took earth from his tomb, mixed it with water, and drank it, saying illness at once recovered—more fresh earth was added, and little by little it became a high mound.
translations.idiomatic: Malaria was rife. People took soil from his grave, mixed it with water, and drank—sickness lifted, they said—and kept adding fresh earth until a high mound rose.

sentences.zh: 徐溫等惡之，發其屍，投於雷公塘。

translations.literal: Xu Wen and the others hated this; they dug up the corpse and cast it into Leigong Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen hated the cult. His men dug up the corpse and threw it into Leigong Pond.

sentences.zh: 後溫病，夢瑾挽弓射之。

translations.literal: Later Wen fell ill and dreamed Jin drawing a bow to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wen fell ill and dreamed Jin drawing a bow on him.

sentences.zh: 溫懼，網其骨，葬塘側，立祠其上。

translations.literal: Wen was afraid, netted the bones, buried them beside the pond, and erected a shrine above.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, he gathered the bones, buried them by the pond, and built a shrine above.

sentences.zh: 初，瑾嘗病疽，醫者視之，色懼，瑾曰：「但理之，吾非以病死者。

translations.literal: Earlier Jin had once suffered a carbuncle; the physician looked at it, his color fearful; Jin said: “Only treat it—I am not one to die by illness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin had a carbuncle. The doctor looked, face white with fear. Jin said: “Treat it. I will not die of sickness.

sentences.zh: 」於是果然。

translations.literal: ” And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: ” And so it was.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 王師範

translations.literal: Wang Shifan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan

sentences.zh: 王師範，青州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan was a native of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan came from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父敬武，為平盧軍牙將。

translations.literal: His father Jingwu was a yamen officer of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingwu was a yamen officer in the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明元年，無棣人洪霸郎為盜齊、棣間，平盧節度使安師儒遣敬武率兵擊破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming of Tang, Hong Balang of Wudi was bandit between Qi and Di; Pinglu’s military governor An Shiru sent Jingwu with troops to break him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang’s first Guangming year (880) Hong Balang of Wudi raided Qi and Di. An Shiru, governor of Pinglu, sent Jingwu to crush him.

sentences.zh: 敬武反，兵逐師儒，自稱留後，都統王鐸承制拜敬武節度使。

translations.literal: Jingwu turned on his troops; the army drove off Shiru, Jingwu styled himself acting governor, and the supreme commander Wang Duo by imperial commission appointed Jingwu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu turned on his own army. The troops expelled Shiru. Jingwu made himself acting governor. Wang Duo, supreme commander, confirmed him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 敬武卒，師範尚幼，其棣州刺史張蟾叛。

translations.literal: Jingwu died; Shifan was still young, and Di prefecture’s governor Zhang Chan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu died while Shifan was still a boy. Zhang Chan, governor of Di prefecture, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 昭宗以為師範年少，其下不服從，乃拜太子少師崔安潛為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong thought Shifan young and that his subordinates would not obey, and appointed the heir apparent’s junior tutor Cui Anqian military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong thought the boy could not hold his men and named Cui Anqian, junior tutor to the heir apparent, governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 師範不受代，蟾迎安潛入棣州。

translations.literal: Shifan would not yield the post; Chan welcomed Anqian into Di prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan refused to step down. Chan brought Anqian into Di prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師範遣其將盧洪攻蟾，洪以兵返襲青州，師范陽為好辭，遣人迎語洪曰：「吾幼未能任事，賴諸將共持之爾。

translations.literal: Shifan sent his general Lu Hong to attack Chan; Hong turned his troops back to strike Qingzhou. Shifan spoke friendly words and sent a man to meet Hong and say: “I am young and cannot yet bear affairs—I rely on you generals to hold them up together.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan sent Lu Hong against Chan. Hong wheeled his army back on Qingzhou. Shifan sent soft words to meet him: “I am young and cannot yet rule. I lean on you generals to hold the domain together.

sentences.zh: 不然，聽公所為也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, do as you will.
translations.idiomatic: If not, do as you please.

sentences.zh: 」洪以師範無能為，遽還，不為備。

translations.literal: ” Hong thought Shifan incapable, hurried back, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hong judged Shifan helpless, marched back at once, and set no guard.

sentences.zh: 師範伏兵於道，語其仆劉鄩曰：「洪來，為我斬之！

translations.literal: Shifan hid troops on the road and told his servant Liu Zan: “When Hong comes, cut him down for me!
translations.idiomatic: Shifan hid men on the road and told his servant Liu Zan: “When Hong comes, strike off his head!

sentences.zh: 用爾為牙將。

translations.literal: I will make you a yamen officer.
translations.idiomatic: I will make you a yamen officer.

sentences.zh: 」明日，洪來，師範出迎，鄩於坐上斬之，伏兵發，盡殺其餘兵，乃急攻棣州，破張蟾，安潛奔歸於京師。

translations.literal: ” The next day Hong came; Shifan went out to meet him, and Zan beheaded him at the seat; the hidden troops sprang forth and killed all the rest of the soldiers, then urgently attacked Di, broke Zhang Chan, and Anqian fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: ” Next day Hong came. Shifan met him at the gate. Zan struck him down at table. The ambush rose and slaughtered the rest, then stormed Di, broke Zhang Chan, and Anqian fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 昭宗乃拜師範節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong then appointed Shifan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong then named Shifan military governor.

sentences.zh: 師範頗好儒學，聚書至萬卷，為政有威愛。

translations.literal: Shifan rather loved Confucian learning, gathered books to ten thousand scrolls, and in governing had both sternness and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan loved the classics, amassed ten thousand scrolls, and ruled with sternness and mercy together.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖圍昭宗於鳳翔，宦官韓全誨等矯詔召諸鎮兵以擊梁。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu besieged Emperor Zhaozong at Fengxiang; the eunuch Han Quanhui and others forged an edict summoning the circuits’ troops to strike Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen besieged Emperor Zhaozong at Fengxiang. The eunuch Han Quanhui forged an edict calling every circuit to march on Liang.

sentences.zh: 詔至青州，師範泣曰：「諸鎮有兵，所以藩捍天子，今天子危辱，而諸鎮反以兵自衛；

translations.literal: When the edict reached Qingzhou, Shifan wept and said: “The circuits have troops to shield and defend the Son of Heaven—today the Son of Heaven is in peril and dishonor, yet the circuits instead use troops to guard themselves;
translations.idiomatic: The edict reached Qingzhou. Shifan wept and said: “Circuits keep armies to shield the Son of Heaven. Now the throne is in peril, and the circuits hide behind their walls instead;

sentences.zh: 吾雖力不足，當成敗以之。

translations.literal: though my strength is insufficient, I shall stake success or failure on it.
translations.idiomatic: my strength is small, but I will stake everything on it.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使乞兵於楊行密。

translations.literal: ” He then sent envoys to beg troops from Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent envoys to beg troops from Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁已東下兗、鄆，師範乃遣劉鄩與其弟師魯分攻兗、密諸州。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had already marched east on Yanzhou and Yunzhou; Shifan then sent Liu Zan and his younger brother Shilu to attack Yan, Mi, and the other prefectures separately.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was already driving east on Yanzhou and Yunzhou. Shifan sent Liu Zan and his brother Shilu against Yan, Mi, and the neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遣張居厚以壯士二百為輿夫，伏兵輿中，西馳梁軍，稱師範使者聘梁，因欲劫殺太祖。

translations.literal: He sent Zhang Juhou with two hundred stalwarts as sedan-bearers, troops hidden in the sedan, galloping west toward Liang’s army, claiming to be Shifan’s envoy paying court to Liang, intending thereby to seize and kill the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Juhou west with two hundred strong men as litter-bearers, weapons hidden in the sedan, galloping toward Liang’s camp as Shifan’s envoy to pay court—and to kill Zhu Wen.

sentences.zh: 居厚至華州東城，華州將婁敬思疑其有異，剖輿視之，見其兵。

translations.literal: Juhou reached Huazhou’s east wall; Huazhou’s officer Lou Jingsi suspected something amiss, cut open the sedan and saw the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Juhou reached Huazhou’s east wall. Lou Jingsi, an officer of Huazhou, smelled a trap, split the sedan open, and found the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 居厚遂擊殺敬思，以兵攻西城，不克而反。

translations.literal: Juhou then struck and killed Jingsi, attacked the west wall with troops, could not take it, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Juhou killed Jingsi, stormed the west wall, failed, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩逐葛從周取兗州，而平盧諸州皆起兵攻梁。

translations.literal: Liu Zan drove Ge Congzhou and took Yanzhou, while all Pinglu’s prefectures rose to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zan drove Ge Congzhou off and took Yanzhou. Every Pinglu prefecture rose against Liang.

sentences.zh: 其後，梁太祖自鳳翔東還，遣朱友寧攻師範，友寧戰死。

translations.literal: Later Liang Taizu returned east from Fengxiang and sent Zhu Youning to attack Shifan; Youning died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen came east from Fengxiang and sent Zhu Youning against Shifan. Youning fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 復遣楊師厚攻之，屯於臨朐。

translations.literal: He again sent Yang Shihou to attack him; Shihou encamped at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Shihou next. Shihou camped at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 師範以兵迫之，師厚陽為怯不敢出，間遣人陽言曰：「梁兵少，方乞兵於鳳翔，今糧且絕，當還軍。

translations.literal: Shifan pressed him with troops; Shihou pretended cowardice and dared not come out, while secretly sending men to speak openly: “Liang’s troops are few; they are just now begging troops from Fengxiang; grain will soon be gone—they must withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan pressed the camp. Shihou played coward, would not fight, and let men spread word: “Liang is weak, begging reinforcements from Fengxiang. Grain is almost gone. They will pull back.

sentences.zh: 」師範以為然，乃遣師魯悉兵攻之，師厚拒而不戰。

translations.literal: ” Shifan believed it and sent Shilu with all his troops to attack; Shihou held the line and would not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shifan believed it and sent Shilu with every man. Shihou shut the gates and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 師魯兵卻，師厚追擊至聖王山，師魯大敗，遂傅其城，而梁別將劉重霸下其棣州，師範乃請降，太祖許之。

translations.literal: Shilu’s troops retreated; Shihou pursued to Shengwang Mountain; Shilu was utterly defeated; Shihou then pressed the city, while Liang’s separate commander Liu Chongba took Di prefecture—Shifan then requested surrender, and the Founder permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu withdrew. Shihou chased him to Shengwang Mountain and broke him utterly, then pressed the city. Liu Chongba took Di prefecture. Shifan sued for peace. Zhu Wen accepted.

sentences.zh: 師範素服乘驢詣太祖請罪，太祖待以客禮。

translations.literal: Shifan in plain dress rode a donkey to the Founder to beg pardon; the Founder received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan came in plain dress on a donkey to beg pardon. Zhu Wen received him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 久之，表師範河陽節度使。

translations.literal: After a long while he memorialized Shifan as military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In time he had Shifan named military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 李罕之

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi

sentences.zh: 李罕之，陳州項城人也。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi was a native of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi was a man of Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 為人驍勇，力兼數人。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and brave, with strength equal to several men.
translations.idiomatic: He was a terror in battle—said to have the strength of several men.

sentences.zh: 少學，讀書不成，去為僧，以其無賴，所往皆不容。

translations.literal: In youth he studied, but reading came to nothing; he left to become a monk, yet because he was unruly, wherever he went none would keep him.
translations.idiomatic: He tried his hand at books as a boy and failed. He took the tonsure, but his rowdiness got him turned out of every monastery that would have him.

sentences.zh: 乃乞食酸棗市中，市中人皆不與，罕之擲器於地，裂其衣，又去為盜。

translations.literal: He then begged for food in the Zaozao market; the people of the market would give him nothing. Hanzhi hurled his bowl to the ground, tore his robes, and went off to become a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: He ended up begging in the Zaozao market. When the townsfolk refused him, he smashed his bowl, ripped off his monk’s robes, and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 是時，黃巢起曹、濮，乃往依之。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Chao rose in Cao and Pu; Hanzhi went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao rose in Cao and Pu, Hanzhi threw in with him.

sentences.zh: 巢北渡江，罕之與其麾下走淮南，自歸於高駢，駢表光州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chao crossed the Yangtze northward, Hanzhi fled with his followers to Huainan and submitted to Gao Pian, who memorialized him as prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chao marched north across the Yangtze. Hanzhi broke away with his men to Huainan and offered himself to Gao Pian, who had him named prefect of Guang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，秦宗權急攻光州，罕之不能守，還走項城，收其餘眾，依諸葛爽於河陽，爽以罕之為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year Qin Zongquan pressed Guangzhou hard; Hanzhi could not hold it. He fled back to Xiangcheng, gathered his remaining troops, and attached himself to Zhuge Shuang at Heyang; Shuang made Hanzhi prefect of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: A year on, Qin Zongquan hammered Guang until Hanzhi could not hold the city. He fell back to Xiangcheng, scraped up what men he had left, and threw in with Zhuge Shuang at Heyang. Shuang gave him Huai.

sentences.zh: 巢已敗走，爽降唐，僖宗拜爽東南面招討使，以攻宗權，爽表罕之副使，以兵屯宋州，又表河南尹、東都留守。

translations.literal: Chao had already been defeated and fled. Shuang surrendered to Tang; Emperor Xizong appointed Shuang southeastern campaign commissioner to attack Zongquan. Shuang memorialized Hanzhi as his deputy, stationed troops at Songzhou, and also memorialized him as Henan governor and eastern capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was already broken and on the run. Shuang came over to Tang, and Xizong made him commissioner to crush Zongquan. Shuang named Hanzhi his deputy, camped him at Song, and had him posted as Henan governor and defender of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權遣孫儒攻河南，罕之兵少，西走澠池，儒燒宮闕，剽掠而去。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan sent Sun Ru to attack Henan. Hanzhi had few troops and fled west to Mianchi. Ru burned the palaces and plundered as he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent Sun Ru against Henan. Outnumbered, Hanzhi fell back west to Mianchi. Ru torched the palace quarter and stripped the region bare on his way out.

sentences.zh: 罕之壁澠池。

translations.literal: Hanzhi fortified Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi dug in at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，諸葛爽死，其將劉經立爽子仲方。

translations.literal: After more than a year Zhuge Shuang died; his officer Liu Jing installed Shuang’s son Zhongfang.
translations.idiomatic: Another year passed and Zhuge Shuang died. His officer Liu Jing put Shuang’s young son Zhongfang in his place.

sentences.zh: 仲方年少，事皆任經，經慮罕之兇勇難制，以兵攻之，罕之返擊走經。

translations.literal: Zhongfang was young; Liu Jing handled everything. Jing feared Hanzhi’s savage courage and that he could not be controlled, and attacked him with troops. Hanzhi turned and struck back, driving Jing off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was a boy; Jing ran the show. Jing feared Hanzhi’s violence and that he could not be tamed, and sent troops against him. Hanzhi wheeled about and routed Jing.

sentences.zh: 罕之追至鞏縣，陳舟於汜水，將渡河，經遣張言拒之河上，言反背經，與罕之合攻河陽，為經所敗，退保懷州。

translations.literal: Hanzhi pursued to Gong County, arrayed boats at Sishui, and was about to cross the river. Jing sent Zhang Yan to block him on the north bank. Yan turned on Jing, joined Hanzhi in attacking Heyang, was defeated by Jing, and fell back to hold Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi chased Jing to Gong, lined boats on the Sishui, and prepared to cross. Jing sent Zhang Yan to hold the north bank. Yan betrayed Jing, joined Hanzhi in a strike on Heyang, was beaten, and pulled back to defend Huai.

sentences.zh: 已而孫儒陷河陽，仲方奔於梁。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Ru took Heyang, and Zhongfang fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Ru seized Heyang, and Zhongfang fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁兵擊走儒，罕之襲取河陽，言取河南，皆附於梁。

translations.literal: Liang troops drove Ru off. Hanzhi seized Heyang; Yan took Henan—both attached themselves to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang forces drove Ru away. Hanzhi snatched Heyang; Yan took Henan. Both men now served Liang.

sentences.zh: 罕之與言皆爽叛將，事已成，乃相與交臂為盟，誓同休戚不相忘。

translations.literal: Hanzhi and Yan were both Shuang’s turncoat generals. Once their business was settled, they locked arms in alliance, swearing to share fortune and misfortune and never forget each other.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi and Yan were both renegades from Shuang’s camp. When the fighting was done, they clasped arms and swore one fortune for both—never to forget the bond.

sentences.zh: 罕之禦眾無法，性苛暴，頗失士心。

translations.literal: Hanzhi had no method in commanding the masses; by nature he was harsh and violent, and he lost the hearts of his officers considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi ruled by terror and had no discipline in camp. His cruelty cost him the loyalty of his men.

sentences.zh: 而言善治軍旅，教民播殖，務為積聚。

translations.literal: Yan, by contrast, was skilled at governing armies, teaching the people to sow and plant, and bent on accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the opposite: a soldier who could run an army and a province—he put people to the plow and hoarded grain for hard times.

sentences.zh: 罕之用兵，言嘗供給其乏。

translations.literal: When Hanzhi took the field, Yan would supply his shortages.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hanzhi marched, Yan fed his shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 罕之求取無已，言頗苦之，不能輸，罕之召言軍吏笞責之，言益不平。

translations.literal: Hanzhi’s demands were endless; Yan grew bitter at it. Unable to keep paying, Hanzhi summoned Yan’s army clerks and had them flogged. Yan grew all the more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi’s demands never stopped. Yan wearied of them. When he could not deliver, Hanzhi had Yan’s supply officers beaten in public. Yan’s resentment turned to hatred.

sentences.zh: 罕之悉兵攻晉、絳，言夜襲河陽，罕之奔晉。

translations.literal: Hanzhi mustered all his troops to attack Jin and Jiang. Yan raided Heyang by night. Hanzhi fled to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi marched in full force on Jin and Jiang. Yan struck Heyang by night. Hanzhi ran to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉表罕之澤州刺史，使李存孝以兵三萬助罕之攻言。

translations.literal: Jin memorialized Hanzhi as prefect of Ze; Li Cunxiao was sent with thirty thousand men to help Hanzhi attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin named him prefect of Ze and sent Li Cunxiao with thirty thousand men to help him crush Yan.

sentences.zh: 言求救於梁。

translations.literal: Yan sought rescue from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan called on Liang for help.

sentences.zh: 罕之敗於沇河，乃歸太原，李克用延之帳中。

translations.literal: Hanzhi was defeated on the Yan River and returned to Taiyuan. Li Keyong received him in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi lost on the Yan River and retreated to Taiyuan. Li Keyong took him into his tent.

sentences.zh: 罕之留其子頎事晉，乃之澤州，日以兵鈔懷、孟間，啖人為食。

translations.literal: Hanzhi left his son Qi to serve Jin and went to Ze, raiding daily between Huai and Meng, eating human flesh.
translations.idiomatic: He left his son Qi at Jin’s court and returned to Ze, raiding Huai and Meng every day—and feeding his men on human flesh.

sentences.zh: 居民屯聚摩雲山，罕之悉攻殺之，立柵其上，時人號曰李摩雲。

translations.literal: The people had gathered on Mount Moyun; Hanzhi attacked and killed them all, built a stockade on the summit, and men of the time called him Li Moyun.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees had crowded Mount Moyun. Hanzhi slaughtered them to the last, threw up a stockade on the peak, and the country took to calling him Li Moyun—Li Who Touches the Clouds.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉方徇地山東，頗倚罕之為捍蔽。

translations.literal: At that time Jin was pushing east through Shandong and leaned heavily on Hanzhi as a shield.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was carving up Shandong and counted on Hanzhi to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞等犯京師，克用以兵至渭北，僖宗以克用為邠州四面行營都統，表罕之為副。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen and others invaded the capital. Keyong brought troops to the north bank of the Wei. Emperor Xizong made Keyong overall commander of the four faces of Binzhou and memorialized Hanzhi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen and his allies struck the capital. Keyong marched to the Wei’s north bank. Xizong named Keyong supreme commander against Bin and made Hanzhi his second.

sentences.zh: 破王行瑜，加檢校太尉，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: They broke Wang Xingyu; Hanzhi was promoted acting Grand Guardian, with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: They shattered Wang Xingyu. Hanzhi was made acting Grand Guardian with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 罕之自以功多於晉，私謂蓋寓曰：「自吾脫身河陽，賴晉容我，未能有以報之；

translations.literal: Hanzhi considered his merit to Jin greater than they acknowledged. Privately he told Gai Yu: “Since I escaped Heyang, I have relied on Jin’s shelter and have not been able to repay it;
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi believed he had done more for Jin than Jin admitted. He told Gai Yu in private: “Jin took me in when I fled Heyang. I have never repaid that debt;

sentences.zh: 今行老矣，無能為也。

translations.literal: now I am old and can do nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: I am old now, and useless.

sentences.zh: 若吾王見憐，與一小鎮，使休兵養疾而後歸老，幸也！

translations.literal: If my lord would pity me with a small commandery, let me rest the troops and nurse my illness, then go home to die in peace—that would be fortune!
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince would grant me some small town, let me stand down my men and heal, then die at home—that would be mercy.

sentences.zh: 」寓為言之，克用不對。

translations.literal: ” Yu spoke for him; Keyong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gai Yu carried the plea to Keyong. Keyong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 佗日，諸鎮擇守將，未嘗及罕之，罕之心益怏怏。

translations.literal: On another day, when the circuits chose garrison commanders, Hanzhi was never named; his heart grew all the more sullen.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the circuits picked new garrison chiefs. Hanzhi’s name was never on the list. His resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 寓告克用，懼罕之有佗心，克用曰：「吾於罕之，豈惜一鎮，然鷹鳥之性，飽則揚矣！」

translations.literal: Yu told Keyong he feared Hanzhi might harbor other designs. Keyong said: “Toward Hanzhi, would I begrudge one commandery? But a hawk’s nature is to fly once it is full!
translations.idiomatic: Yu warned Keyong that Hanzhi might turn disloyal. Keyong said: “I would not begrudge him a town—but a hawk flies once its belly is full.

sentences.zh: 罕之初背梁而歸晉，晉王以罕之守澤州，罕之留其子頎與莊宗遊，甚狎。

translations.literal: When Hanzhi first deserted Liang for Jin, the Prince of Jin had Hanzhi hold Ze while Hanzhi left his son Qi to keep company with the Heir Zhuangzong—they were very intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanzhi first left Liang for Jin, Keyong put him in Ze and left his son Qi at Taiyuan with the heir Li Cunxu—they were thick as kin.

sentences.zh: 後罕之背晉以歸梁，晉王怒，欲殺頎，莊宗與之駿馬，使奔於梁。

translations.literal: Later, when Hanzhi deserted Jin for Liang, the Prince of Jin was furious and wished to kill Qi. Zhuangzong gave him a fine horse and sent him galloping to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanzhi later betrayed Jin for Liang, Keyong wanted Qi dead. Li Cunxu gave the boy a swift horse and sent him racing to Liang.

sentences.zh: 太祖得頎父子大喜，使與友倫將兵以衛昭宗，故頎當太祖時，常掌禁兵。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was overjoyed to have Qi and his father. He had them serve with Youlun in guarding Emperor Zhaozong; thus under the Founding Emperor Qi often held the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted to have father and son. He paired Qi with Zhu Youlun to guard Zhaozong, and Qi spent those years commanding the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 末帝誅友珪，頎與其謀，拜右羽林統軍、澶州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor killed Yougui, Qi took part in the plot and was made Right Imperial Guard commander and prefect of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor killed Zhu Yougui, Qi helped plot it and was made commander of the Right Imperial Guard and prefect of Cao.

sentences.zh: 事唐，歷衛、衍二州刺史，累遷右領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Serving Tang, he held the prefectures of Wei and Yan in succession and rose to Right Leader of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang he governed Wei and Yan in turn and rose to Right Leader of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天福中卒，年七十，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died in the Tianfu era at seventy; posthumously he was made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Tianfu reign at seventy and was posthumously made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 孟方立

translations.literal: Meng Fangli
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli

sentences.zh: 孟方立，邢州平鄉人也。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli was a native of Pingxiang in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli was a man of Pingxiang in Xing.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒，以勇力選為隊將。

translations.literal: In youth he was a common soldier; for courage and strength he was chosen as a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a common soldier and was picked to lead a company for his strength.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明中，潞州節度使高潯攻諸葛爽於河陽，遣方立將兵出天井關為先鋒。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era of Tang, Gao Xun, military governor of Luzhou, attacked Zhuge Shuang at Heyang and sent Fangli with troops out through Tianjing Pass as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang’s Guangming era Gao Xun of Luzhou marched on Zhuge Shuang at Heyang and sent Fangli through Tianjing Pass at the head of the column.

sentences.zh: 潯為其將劉廣所逐，廣為亂軍所殺。

translations.literal: Xun was driven off by his officer Liu Guang; Guang was killed by the mutinous army.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was overthrown by his officer Liu Guang; the mutineers then killed Guang.

sentences.zh: 方立聞亂，引兵自天井入據潞州，唐因以為昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Hearing of the turmoil, Fangli led his troops in through Tianjing and seized Luzhou; Tang thereupon appointed him military governor of the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the chaos, Fangli marched back through Tianjing and took Luzhou. Tang named him governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 昭義所節制澤、潞、邢、洺、磁五州，而治潞州。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi governed Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci—five prefectures—with its seat at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi held Ze, Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci—five prefectures—from its seat at Lu.

sentences.zh: 方立以謂潞州山川高險，而人俗勁悍，自劉積以來嘗逐其帥；

translations.literal: Fangli judged that Luzhou’s mountains were high and its passes dangerous, its people fierce and stubborn; since Liu Zong’s day its governors had often been driven out;
translations.idiomatic: Fangli decided Lu was all cliffs and hard country, its people violent and proud—since Liu Zong, governors had been thrown out as often as installed;

sentences.zh: 且己邢人也，因徙其軍於邢州。

translations.literal: and he himself was a man of Xing; he therefore moved his army to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and he was a Xing man himself. He shifted his army to Xing.

sentences.zh: 而潞人怨方立之徙也，因以澤、潞二州歸於晉。

translations.literal: The people of Lu resented Fangli’s move; they therefore gave Ze and Lu to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu resented the move. Ze and Lu went over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉遣李克修為澤潞節度使，方立以邢、洺、磁三州自為昭義軍。

translations.literal: Jin sent Li Kexiu as military governor of Ze and Lu; Fangli kept Xing, Ming, and Ci as his own Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Li Kexiu to hold Ze and Lu. Fangli kept Xing, Ming, and Ci and called them Zhaoyi still.

sentences.zh: 方立將石元佐者，善兵而多智，方立嘗信用之。

translations.literal: Fangli’s general Shi Yuankuo was skilled in war and full of stratagems; Fangli often trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli’s officer Shi Yuankuo knew war and scheming; Fangli leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 忠信之敗也，元佐為晉將安金俊所得，金俊厚遇之，問以攻邢之策，元佐曰：「方立善守而邢城堅，若攻之，必不得志。

translations.literal: At Xi Zhongxin’s defeat, Yuankuo was taken by Jin’s officer An Jinjun. Jinjun treated him generously and asked his plan for attacking Xing. Yuankuo said: “Fangli is good at defense and Xing’s walls are strong; if you attack it, you will certainly not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi Zhongxin’s defeat, Yuankuo fell into the hands of Jin’s An Jinjun. Jinjun treated him well and asked how to take Xing. Yuankuo said: “Fangli is a stubborn defender and Xing’s walls are high. A direct assault will fail.

sentences.zh: 宜急攻其磁州，方立來救，可以敗也。

translations.literal: You should strike Ci in haste; when Fangli comes to the rescue, you can defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Hit Ci hard and fast. When Fangli rushes to save it, you can break him in the field.

sentences.zh: 」金俊以為然。

translations.literal: ” Jinjun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jinjun took the advice.

sentences.zh: 軍於滏水之西，方立果帥兵來救，為金俊所敗，馳入邢州，閉壁不復出。

translations.literal: He encamped west of the Fushui. Fangli indeed led troops to the rescue and was defeated by Jinjun, galloping into Xingzhou, shutting the walls, and never coming out again.
translations.idiomatic: Jinjun camped west of the Fushui. Fangli came as predicted, was smashed, and bolted into Xing. He barred the gates and would not fight again.

sentences.zh: 外無救兵，城中食且盡，方立夜出巡城，號令守者，守者皆不應，方立知不可，乃歸飲鴆而卒。

translations.literal: With no relief from outside and food in the city nearly gone, Fangli went out at night to tour the walls and call orders to the defenders; the defenders would not answer. Fangli knew it was hopeless, returned, drank poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: No help came. The granaries ran dry. Fangli walked the walls at night, shouting orders; no one answered. He knew the game was over, went home, and drank poison.

sentences.zh: 王珂，河中人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ke was a native of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke was a man of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 其仲父重榮，以河中兵破黃巢，有功於唐，拜河中節度使。

translations.literal: His uncle Chongrong, with Hezhong troops, broke Huang Chao and had merit toward Tang; he was made military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Wang Chongrong had smashed Huang Chao with Hezhong’s army and earned Tang’s gratitude; Tang made him governor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 重榮無子，以其兄重簡子珂為後。

translations.literal: Chongrong had no sons and took his elder brother Chongjian’s son Ke as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong had no sons. He adopted Chongjian’s boy Ke as his heir.

sentences.zh: 重榮卒，弟重盈立，重盈卒，軍中乃以珂重榮子，立之。

translations.literal: Chongrong died; his younger brother Chongying succeeded. When Chongying died, the army took Ke as Chongrong’s son and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong died; his brother Chongying followed him. When Chongying died, the army declared Ke Chongrong’s true heir and raised him up.

sentences.zh: 重盈子陜州節度使珙、絳州刺史瑤，與珂爭立，珙、瑤以書與梁太祖，言珂故王氏蒼頭，小字忠兒，不應得立。

translations.literal: Chongying’s sons—Gong, military governor of Shaan, and Yao, prefect of Jiang—contested Ke’s succession. Gong and Yao wrote Liang’s Founding Emperor saying Ke was formerly a Wang family bondservant, childhood name Zhong’er, and ought not to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying’s sons Gong of Shaan and Yao of Jiang fought Ke for the seat. They wrote Taizu that Ke had been a Wang household bondservant—pet name Zhong’er—and had no claim.

sentences.zh: 珂亦求援於晉，晉人言之朝，昭宗以晉故，許之。

translations.literal: Ke also sought aid from Jin; Jin’s men spoke for him at court, and because of Jin, Emperor Zhaozong permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ke appealed to Jin. Jin’s envoys pleaded at court, and for Jin’s sake Zhaozong assented.

sentences.zh: 而珙、瑤亦西結王行瑜、韓建、李茂貞為援，行瑜等交章論列，昭宗報以重榮與晉於唐嘗有大功，業許之，不可易。

translations.literal: Gong and Yao also allied west with Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Li Maozhen. Xingyu and the others sent memorial after memorial arguing the case. Zhaozong replied that Chongrong and Jin had once rendered great service to Tang; the throne had promised—this could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Yao also courted Wang Xingyu, Han Jian, and Li Maozhen in the west. Memorials flooded the throne. Zhaozong answered that Chongrong and Jin had saved Tang once; the promise stood—it would not be undone.

sentences.zh: 行瑜等怒，以兵犯京師，殺宰相李磎等而去。

translations.literal: Xingyu and the others were enraged; they brought troops against the capital, killed the chief minister Li Xi and others, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and his allies marched on the capital in fury, murdered Chief Minister Li Xi and others, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 珙、瑤連兵攻珂河中，珂求援於晉，晉兵西討三鎮，行下絳州，斬瑤而過，至於渭北，擊破行瑜。

translations.literal: Gong and Yao joined forces to attack Ke in Hezhong. Ke sought aid from Jin; Jin’s army marched west against the three circuits, took Jiang on the way and beheaded Yao, reached the north bank of the Wei, and broke Xingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Yao besieged Ke in Hezhong. Ke called Jin. Jin marched west against the three allies, cut down Yao at Jiang on the way, reached the Wei’s north bank, and shattered Xingyu.

sentences.zh: 昭宗卒以珂為河中節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong at last made Ke military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At last Zhaozong confirmed Ke as governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 晉以女妻之，遣李嗣昭將兵助珂攻珙陜州。

translations.literal: Jin gave him a daughter in marriage and sent Li Sizhao with troops to help Ke attack Gong at Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin gave him a princess and sent Li Sizhao to help him take Shaan from Gong.

sentences.zh: 珙為人慘刻，嘗斬人擲其首於前，言笑自若，其下苦之。

translations.literal: Gong was cruel by nature; he would behead a man and toss the head before him, then talk and laugh as if nothing had happened—his subordinates suffered bitterly under him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was vicious. He would cut off a man’s head and set it on the table while he joked over wine. His officers hated him.

sentences.zh: 偏將李璠因珙戰敗，殺珙，自稱留後。

translations.literal: The subordinate officer Li Fan, because Gong was defeated in battle, killed Gong and declared himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong lost a battle, his officer Li Fan killed him and named himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁已下鎮、定，將移兵西，而昭宗為劉季述所廢，京師大亂。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had already taken Zhen and Ding and was about to shift troops west, but Emperor Zhaozong had been deposed by Liu Jishu and the capital was in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had taken Zhen and Ding and was turning west when Liu Jishu deposed Zhaozong and the capital dissolved into chaos.

sentences.zh: 崔胤陰召梁以兵西，梁太祖以珂在河中，懼為患，乃顧張存敬、侯言，以一大繩與之，曰：「為我持縛珂來！

translations.literal: Cui Yin secretly summoned Liang’s troops west. The Founding Emperor, fearing Ke in Hezhong as a future trouble, turned to Zhang Cunjing and Hou Yan and gave them a great rope, saying: “Bring Ke to me bound!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin quietly called Liang west. Taizu feared Ke in Hezhong and turned to Zhang Cunjing and Hou Yan with a heavy rope. “Bind Ke and bring him to me,

sentences.zh: 」存敬等兵出含山，破晉、絳二州，遣何絪以兵守之，絕晉援。

translations.literal: ” Cunjing and the others marched out from Hanshan, broke Jin and Jiang, and sent He Yin with troops to hold them, cutting off Jin’s relief.
translations.idiomatic: ” he said. Cunjing marched from Hanshan, overran Jin and Jiang, and posted He Yin to choke off relief from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 存敬圍河中，珂告急於晉，晉以絪故不得前。

translations.literal: Cunjing besieged Hezhong. Ke sent urgent word to Jin, but because of He Yin, Jin could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing tightened the siege. Ke begged Jin for rescue, but He Yin’s blockade held the Jin army still.

sentences.zh: 珂乃遣其妻以書告晉王曰：「賊勢如此，朝夕乞食於梁矣！

translations.literal: Ke then had his wife write the Prince of Jin: “The enemy’s strength is such that we will soon be begging food from Liang!
translations.idiomatic: Ke had his wife write Keyong: “The enemy is this strong—we will soon be eating Liang’s scraps!

sentences.zh: 大人何忍而不救邪？

translations.literal: How can my lord bear not to save us?
translations.idiomatic: My lord, how can you leave us to die?

sentences.zh: 」晉王報之曰：「梁兵為阻，眾寡不敵，救之則並晉俱亡，不若與王郎自歸朝廷。

translations.literal: ” The Prince of Jin replied: “Liang’s troops block the way; we are too few to match them. If we rescue you, Jin and Hezhong perish together. Better that you and Lord Wang surrender to the court yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: ” Keyong answered: “Liang blocks the road. We are too few. If I march, Jin and Hezhong fall together. Better you surrender to the throne on your own.

sentences.zh: 」珂乃為書與李茂貞曰：「天子初返正，詔藩鎮無相侵以安王室。

translations.literal: ” Ke then wrote Li Maozhen: “The Son of Heaven has just been restored; he has decreed that the circuits must not invade one another so as to secure the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ke wrote Li Maozhen: “The Son of Heaven has only just been restored. He ordered the circuits not to tear at one another—to keep the house of Tang whole.

sentences.zh: 今朱公棄約以見攻，其勢不止於弊邑；

translations.literal: Now Lord Zhu has broken the pact and attacks us; his ambition will not stop at our little circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu Wen breaks the pact and strikes us. He will not stop at our one circuit;

sentences.zh: 若弊邑朝亡，則西北諸鎮非諸君所能守也！

translations.literal: if our circuit falls tomorrow, the northwest circuits will not be yours to hold!
translations.idiomatic: if we fall tomorrow, you will not hold the northwest.

sentences.zh: 願與華州出兵潼關以為應。

translations.literal: I beg you and Huazhou to march out through Tong Pass in support.
translations.idiomatic: March from Huazhou through Tong Pass and meet me.

sentences.zh: 」茂貞不報。

translations.literal: ” Maozhen did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: ” Maozhen never answered.

sentences.zh: 珂計窮，乃治舟於河，將歸於京師。

translations.literal: Ke’s plans exhausted, he prepared boats on the river, intending to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Out of options, Ke fitted boats on the river to flee to the capital.

sentences.zh: 珂夜登城諭守陴者，守陴者皆不應。

translations.literal: At night Ke mounted the wall to address the defenders on the parapet; the defenders would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: That night he climbed the wall and called to the men on the battlements. No one answered.

sentences.zh: 牙將劉訓夜入珂寢白事，珂叱之曰：「兵欲反邪！

translations.literal: The guard officer Liu Xun entered Ke’s quarters at night to report business. Ke shouted at him: “Do the troops mean to rebel?
translations.idiomatic: His guard officer Liu Xun came to Ke’s chamber at night on business. Ke snapped: “Are my soldiers mutinying?

sentences.zh: 」訓乃解衣自索而入曰：「公茍懷疑，請先斷臂！

translations.literal: ” Xun then stripped off his upper garment, bound his own arms, and entered, saying: “If my lord still doubts, cut off my arm first!
translations.idiomatic: ” Xun tore off his jacket, bound his own arms, and stepped in. “If you still doubt me, take my arm first.

sentences.zh: 」珂曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: ” Ke said: “The matter is urgent!
translations.idiomatic: ” Ke said: “We are out of time.

sentences.zh: 計安出乎？

translations.literal: What plan can we use?
translations.idiomatic: What is left to do?

sentences.zh: 」訓曰：「公若攜家夜濟，人必爭舟，一夫鴟張，大事即去。

translations.literal: ” Xun said: “If my lord takes his household across the river by night, men will fight over the boats; one man’s arrogance and the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xun said: “If you put your family in boats tonight, men will fight for the planks. One panic and everything is gone.

sentences.zh: 不若遲明以情諭軍中，願從者猶得其半。

translations.literal: Better wait until dawn and speak plainly to the army—those willing to follow may still be half.
translations.idiomatic: Wait for dawn. Speak to the army honestly—perhaps half will still follow you.

sentences.zh: 不然，且為款狀以緩梁兵，徐圖向背。

translations.literal: If not, at least make a show of surrender to slow Liang’s troops, and plot your course afterward.
translations.idiomatic: If not, feign surrender to buy time, then choose your side.

sentences.zh: 」珂以為然。

translations.literal: ” Ke agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ke agreed.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖自同州降唐，即依重榮，以母王氏，故事重榮為舅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor had surrendered to Tang from Tongzhou, he had attached himself to Chongrong; because his mother was surnamed Wang, by custom he treated Chongrong as maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu came over to Tang from Tong, he had clung to Chongrong. His mother was a Wang by birth, so by custom he called Chongrong uncle.

sentences.zh: 珂乃登城呼存敬曰：「吾於梁王有家世之舊，兵當退舍，俟梁王來，吾將聽命。

translations.literal: Ke then mounted the wall and called to Cunjing: “I and Lord Liang have old family ties—the army ought to withdraw. Wait until Lord Liang comes; I will obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Ke climbed the wall and shouted to Cunjing: “Taizu and I are family. Pull your men back. When he comes, I will yield to him.

sentences.zh: 」存敬乃退舍，使馳詣太祖於洛陽。

translations.literal: ” Cunjing thereupon withdrew his camp and sent a rider posthaste to the Founding Emperor at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Cunjing lifted the siege and galloped a messenger to Taizu in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖至河中，先之城東，哭於重榮之墓而後入。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor reached Hezhong, first went to the east of the city, wept at Chongrong’s tomb, and then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reached Hezhong, wept at Chongrong’s tomb east of the city, and only then went in.

sentences.zh: 珂欲面縛牽羊以見太祖，太祖謂曰：「太師阿舅之恩何時可忘，郎君若以亡國之禮見，太師其謂我何？

translations.literal: Ke wished to present himself bound, leading a sheep—the rite of a fallen state. The Founding Emperor said: “When can I forget Grand Mentor’s kindness as maternal uncle? If you greet me with the rites of a destroyed state, what will the Grand Mentor think of me?
translations.idiomatic: Ke meant to come out bound, leading a sheep—the rite of a conquered prince. Taizu said: “Your uncle’s kindness—I could never forget it. If you greet me like a dead kingdom, what would he think of me?

sentences.zh: 」珂迎於路，握手噓唏，乃徙珂於汴。

translations.literal: ” Ke met him on the road; they clasped hands and wept, and Ke was then moved to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ke met him on the road. They clasped hands and wept. Then Ke was sent to Bian.

sentences.zh: 太祖以珂晉婿也，疑其貳己，使珂西入覲，行至華州，使人殺之傳舍。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Ke was Jin’s son-in-law, suspected he would turn against him and had Ke go west to pay court; when he reached Huazhou, men were sent to kill him at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu still feared Ke—he was Jin’s son-in-law—and ordered him west to pay homage. At Huazhou, assassins cut him down in the post house.

sentences.zh: 瓚，重盈之諸子也，梁太祖已執珂，自領河中節度使，以瓚為吏。

translations.literal: Zan was one of Chongying’s younger sons. After Liang Taizu had seized Ke, he took the Hezhong military commission himself and made Zan a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was a younger son of Wang Chongying. Once Taizu had taken Wang Ke, he kept Hezhong for himself and set Zan to clerical work.

sentences.zh: 瓚事梁，為諸衛大將軍，泰寧、鎮國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zan served Liang as grand general of the various guards and as military commissioner of the Taining and Zhenguo armies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he rose to grand general of the guards and military commissioner of Taining and Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 末帝時，為開封尹。

translations.literal: In the time of the Last Emperor he was prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Emperor he governed Kaifeng as its prefect.

sentences.zh: 貞明五年，代賀瑰為北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenming he replaced He Gui as northern campaign commissioner for suppressing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 5 (919) he replaced He Gui as northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉已城德勝，瓚自黎陽渡河攻澶州，不克，退屯楊村，扼河上流，與晉人相持經年，大小百餘戰，瓚卒無功，末帝遣戴思遠代，瓚復為開封尹。

translations.literal: At that time Jin had already fortified Desheng. Zan crossed the Yellow River from Liyang to attack Cangzhou but could not take it; he withdrew and encamped at Yangcun, blocking the upper river. He and the Jin forces faced one another for more than a year, fighting over a hundred engagements large and small, yet Zan in the end achieved nothing. The Last Emperor sent Dai Siyuan to replace him, and Zan again became prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had already walled Desheng. Zan crossed from Liyang to strike Cangzhou, failed, and fell back to Yangcun to choke the upper river. For a year he traded blows with Jin in more than a hundred fights and won nothing. The court sent Dai Siyuan in his place; Zan returned to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 莊宗自鄆入京師，末帝聞唐兵且至，日夜涕泣，不知所為，自持國寶，指其宮室謂瓚曰：「使吾保此者，系卿之畫如何耳！

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered the capital from Yan, the Last Emperor heard that Tang troops were near and wept day and night, not knowing what to do. He took the imperial treasures in hand, pointed at his palace halls, and said to Zan: “Whether I can keep these depends on your plan!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong marched on the capital from Yan. The Last Emperor heard Tang was coming and wept for days, clutching the regalia and pointing at his halls. “Whether I keep any of this,” he told Zan, “is in your hands!

sentences.zh: 」唐兵已過宛朐，瓚驅率市人登城拒守。

translations.literal: ” Tang troops had already passed Wanyu; Zan drove the townspeople onto the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tang had already passed Wanyu. Zan pressed the market folk onto the battlements.

sentences.zh: 唐兵攻封丘門，瓚開門迎降，伏地請死，莊宗勞而起之曰：「朕與卿家世婚姻，然人臣各為主耳，復何罪邪！

translations.literal: Tang troops attacked the Fengqiu Gate. Zan opened the gate to welcome surrender, prostrated himself and begged for death. Zhuangzong comforted him and raised him up, saying: “My house and yours have been joined by marriage for generations; yet each minister serves his own lord—what crime is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: Tang struck the Fengqiu Gate. Zan opened it, threw himself down, and asked to die. Zhuangzong lifted him up. “Our houses have married for generations,” he said. “You served your lord—I see no crime in that.

sentences.zh: 」因以為開封尹，遷宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: ” He thereupon made him prefect of Kaifeng and later transferred him to military commissioner of the Xuanwu army.
translations.idiomatic: ” He made Zan prefect of Kaifeng, then military commissioner of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 已而故梁臣趙巖、張漢傑等相次誅死，瓚以憂卒。

translations.literal: Before long former Liang ministers Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie were executed one after another; Zan died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon former Liang ministers such as Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie were put to death in turn. Zan died of grief.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 趙犨，其先青州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou—his ancestors were natives of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou’s family came from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 世為陳州牙將。

translations.literal: For generations they had been petty officers of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they served Chen Prefecture as yamen soldiers.

sentences.zh: 犨幼與群兒戲道中，部分行伍，指顧如將帥，雖諸大兒皆聽其節度，其父叔文見之，驚曰：「大吾門者，此兒也！

translations.literal: As a child Chou played in the road with other boys, arraying ranks and gesturing like a commander; even the older lads obeyed his orders. His father Shuwen saw it and exclaimed: “The one who will magnify our house is this boy!
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Chou drilled other children in the street like a general; even the older boys took his orders. His father Shuwen stared and said: “This child will raise our house!

sentences.zh: 」及壯，善用弓劍，為人勇果，重氣義，刺史聞其材，召置麾下。

translations.literal: ” When he grew up he was skilled with bow and sword, brave and resolute, and prized honor; the prefect heard of his talent and summoned him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: ” Grown, he was deadly with bow and blade, bold and loyal. The prefect heard of him and took him into his service.

sentences.zh: 累遷忠武軍馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief inspector of the Zhongwu army’s horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief inspector of the Zhongwu army’s horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 王仙芝寇河南，陷汝州，將犯東都，犨引兵擊敗之，仙芝乃南去。

translations.literal: When Wang Xianzhi raided Henan and took Ru Prefecture, about to invade the eastern capital, Chou led troops and defeated him; Xianzhi then turned south.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xianzhi swept Henan, took Ru, and marched on Luoyang. Chou met him and broke his army; Xianzhi turned south.

sentences.zh: 已而黃巢起，所在州縣，往往陷賊。

translations.literal: Before long Huang Chao rose, and prefectures and counties everywhere often fell to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huang Chao rose, and town after town fell to him.

sentences.zh: 陳州豪傑數百人，相與詣忠武軍，求得犨為刺史以自保，忠武軍表犨陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Several hundred Chen notables together went to the Zhongwu army and begged to have Chou made prefect for their own protection; the Zhongwu army memorialized Chou as prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of Chen gentry went to the Zhongwu command and asked for Chou as their prefect. The army so memorialized, and Chou was made prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 已而巢陷長安，犨語諸將吏曰：「以吾計，巢若不為長安市人所誅，必驅其眾東走，吾州適當其沖矣！

translations.literal: Before long Chao took Chang’an. Chou told his officers and clerks: “By my reckoning, if Chao is not killed by the people of Chang’an, he will surely drive his masses east—and our prefecture lies straight in his path!
translations.idiomatic: Chao took Chang’an. Chou told his staff: “If the Chang’an people do not kill him, he will drive east—and Chen lies in his path!

sentences.zh: 」乃治城池為守備，遷民六十里內者皆入城中，選其子弟，配以兵甲，以其弟昶、珝為將。

translations.literal: ” He then repaired the walls and prepared defenses, moved everyone within sixty li into the city, chose their young men, armed them, and made his brothers Chang and Xu his generals.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rebuilt the walls, pulled every soul within sixty li inside, armed the young men, and put his brothers Chang and Xu in command.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，果東走，先遣孟楷據項城，昶擊破之，執楷以歸。

translations.literal: When Chao was defeated he indeed fled east, first sending Meng Kai to seize Xiangcheng. Chang struck and broke him, captured Kai, and brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: Chao broke and ran east, sending Meng Kai to take Xiangcheng. Chang shattered him, took Kai prisoner, and marched him in.

sentences.zh: 巢從後至，聞楷被執，大怒。

translations.literal: Chao came after him, heard Kai had been captured, and was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Chao followed, learned Kai was taken, and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 既而秦宗權以蔡州附巢，巢勢甚盛，乃悉眾圍犨，置舂磨，糜人之肉以為食。

translations.literal: Before long Qin Zongquan of Cai Prefecture joined Chao; Chao’s power grew very strong. He then mustered all his forces to besiege Chou, set up mortars, and ground human flesh for food.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan of Cai threw in with Chao, and Chao’s strength swelled. He surrounded Chen with his whole host, set up pounding mills, and fed his men on ground human flesh.

sentences.zh: 陳人恐，犨語其下曰：「吾家三世陳將，必能保此。

translations.literal: The people of Chen were afraid. Chou told his men: “My house has been Chen’s generals for three generations—we can surely hold this place.
translations.idiomatic: Terror spread through Chen. Chou told his men: “Three generations of my house have defended Chen. We can hold it.

sentences.zh: 爾曹男子，當於死中求生，建功立業，未必不因此時。

translations.literal: You men—seek life in death, win merit and establish your names; it may well be that this is your hour.
translations.idiomatic: You are men. Win your lives from death, make your names—this siege may be your chance.

sentences.zh: 」陳人皆踴躍。

translations.literal: ” The people of Chen all leapt to it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The town answered with a roar.

sentences.zh: 巢柵城北三里為八仙營，起宮闕，置百官，聚糧餉，欲以久弊之，其兵號二十萬。

translations.literal: Chao pitched his Eight Immortals Camp three li north of the walls, raised palaces and halls, installed officials, gathered grain and fodder, and meant to wear them down by a long siege; his army was said to number two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chao built the Eight Immortals Camp three li north of the walls, threw up halls, named officials, stockpiled grain, and settled in for a long war of attrition. His host was said to be two hundred thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 陳人舊有巨弩數百，皆廢壞，後生弩工皆不識其器。

translations.literal: Chen had once possessed several hundred great crossbows, all ruined; the younger craftsmen no longer knew the machines.
translations.idiomatic: Chen once had hundreds of great crossbows, all broken; the young smiths no longer knew how to build them.

sentences.zh: 珝創意理之，弩矢激五百步，人馬皆洞，以故巢不敢近。

translations.literal: Xu devised a way to restore them; their bolts flew five hundred paces and pierced men and horses through. For this reason Chao did not dare come near.
translations.idiomatic: Xu figured out how to repair them. Their bolts tore five hundred paces and punched through men and horses alike. Chao would not come close.

sentences.zh: 圍凡三百日，犨食將盡，乃乞兵於梁。

translations.literal: The siege lasted three hundred days in all; when Chou’s food was nearly gone he begged troops from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The siege ran three hundred days. When grain ran low Chou begged Liang for relief.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖與李克用皆自將會陳，擊敗巢將黃鄴於西華。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu and Li Keyong both led armies in person to Chen and defeated Chao’s general Huang Ye at Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Li Keyong both marched on Chen in person and broke Chao’s general Huang Ye at Xihua.

sentences.zh: 西華有積粟，巢恃以為餉，及鄴敗，巢乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Xihua held stored grain on which Chao had relied for supplies; when Ye was defeated Chao lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xihua held the granaries Chao lived on. Ye’s defeat broke the siege; Chao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖入陳州，犨兄弟迎謁馬首甚恭。

translations.literal: When Liang Taizu entered Chen Prefecture, Chou and his brothers met him at his horse’s head with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu entered Chen. Chou and his brothers met him at the stirrup with deep courtesy.

sentences.zh: 然犨陰識太祖必成大事，乃降心屈跡，為自托之計。

translations.literal: Yet Chou secretly knew Taizu would achieve great things; he lowered himself and bent his pride, scheming to attach himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chou had already read Taizu’s future. He humbled himself and courted him, planning how to bind his house to Liang.

sentences.zh: 以梁援己恩，為太祖立生祠，朝夕拜謁。

translations.literal: Because Liang had rescued him, he built Taizu a living shrine and bowed to it morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Liang’s rescue, he raised a living shrine to Taizu and bowed there every dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 以其子巖尚太祖女，是謂長樂公主。

translations.literal: He gave his son Yan in marriage to Taizu’s daughter—the Princess of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He married his son Yan to Taizu’s daughter, the Princess of Changle.

sentences.zh: 黃巢已去，秦宗權復亂淮西，陷旁二十餘州，而陳去蔡最近，犨兄弟力拒之，卒不能下。

translations.literal: After Chao had gone, Qin Zongquan again threw the Huai west into chaos and seized more than twenty neighboring prefectures. Chen lay closest to Cai, and Chou and his brothers resisted with all their strength; in the end Zongquan could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was gone, but Qin Zongquan ravaged the Huai west and swallowed twenty-odd prefectures. Chen lay nearest Cai; the brothers held the line and Zongquan never took the city.

sentences.zh: 後巢、宗權皆敗死，唐昭宗即以陳州為忠武軍，拜犨節度使。

translations.literal: Later Chao and Zongquan were both defeated and died. Tang Zhaozong made Chen the Zhongwu army and appointed Chou its military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and Zongquan fell and died. Zhaozong made Chen the Zhongwu command and Chou its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 犨已病，乃以位與其弟昶，後數月卒。

translations.literal: Chou was already ill; he gave his post to his brother Chang, and several months later died.
translations.idiomatic: Chou fell ill, handed the seal to Chang, and died a few months later.

sentences.zh: 昶乘大寇新滅，乃休兵課農，事梁尤謹。

translations.literal: Chang, while the great bandits had only just been destroyed, rested the troops and urged the farmers back to the fields, and served Liang with especial care.
translations.idiomatic: With the great rebels barely gone, Chang rested his men and put the farmers back to the fields, serving Liang with meticulous loyalty.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻戰四方，昶饋免供億，未嘗少懈。

translations.literal: As Liang’s armies fought on every front, Chang supplied grain and goods without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Liang fought on every front; Chang fed and equipped its armies without a day’s lapse.

sentences.zh: 昶卒，珝代立。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Xu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang died; Xu took his place.

sentences.zh: 珝頗知書，乃求鄧艾故跡，決翟王陂溉民田。

translations.literal: Xu was quite learned; he sought out Deng Ai’s old traces and opened the Zhaiwang Embankment to irrigate the people’s fields.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was a reader. He traced Deng Ai’s old works, broke open the Zhaiwang Embankment, and watered the fields.

sentences.zh: 兄弟居陳二十餘年，陳人大賴之。

translations.literal: The brothers held Chen for more than twenty years, and the people of Chen relied on them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years the brothers held Chen, and the people prospered under them.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖已降韓建，取同、華，徙珝為同州留後。

translations.literal: After Liang Taizu had reduced Han Jian and taken Tong and Hua, he moved Xu to acting governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu had broken Han Jian and taken Tong and Hua, he shifted Xu to acting governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 入唐，為右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Under Tang he became general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang he rose to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免官歸，卒於家，陳人為之罷市。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed for illness and returned home, dying there; the people of Chen closed their markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A year later illness ended his office; he went home and died. Chen closed its markets in grief.

sentences.zh: 犨次子巖，梁末帝時為戶部尚書、租庸使，與張漢傑、漢倫等居中用事。

translations.literal: Chou’s second son Yan, in the time of the Last Emperor, was Minister of Revenue and commissioner for transport and tax, and with Zhang Hanjie, Han Lun, and others held power at court.
translations.idiomatic: Chou’s second son Yan, under the Last Emperor, was Minister of Revenue and transport commissioner; with Zhang Hanjie, Han Lun, and others he ruled from the center.

sentences.zh: 梁自太祖以暴虐殺戮為事，而末帝為人特和柔恭謹，然性庸愚，以漢傑婦家，而巖婿也，故親信之，大臣老將皆切齒，末帝獨不悟，以至於亡。

translations.literal: From the Founder on, Liang had made violent slaughter its way; the Last Emperor in person was mild, respectful, and cautious by nature, yet foolish and dull. Because Hanjie was his wife’s kin and Yan his son-in-law, he trusted them alone; veteran ministers and generals gnashed their teeth, yet the Last Emperor alone did not wake—until ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: From the Founder, Liang had ruled by the blade. The Last Emperor was gentle and timid by nature, but dull. He favored Hanjie as kin by marriage and Yan as son-in-law; old soldiers and ministers seethed while he slept on—until the house fell.

sentences.zh: 初，友珪殺太祖自立，以末帝為東都留守。

translations.literal: At first Yougui murdered the Founder and seized the throne himself, making the Last Emperor eastern-capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui murdered the Founder and usurped the throne, he left the Last Emperor as garrison commander of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 巖如東都，末帝與之飲酒，從容以誠款告之。

translations.literal: Yan went to the eastern capital; the Last Emperor drank with him and, at ease, spoke to him with sincere trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yan visited the eastern capital. Over wine the Last Emperor opened his heart to him.

sentences.zh: 巖為末帝謀，遣人召楊師厚兵起事。

translations.literal: Yan plotted for the Last Emperor and sent men to summon Yang Shihou’s troops to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan laid plans for him and called Yang Shihou’s army to revolt.

sentences.zh: 巖還西都，卒與袁象先以禁兵誅友珪，取傳國寶以授末帝。

translations.literal: Yan returned to the western capital and at last, with Yuan Xiangxian, used the palace guard to kill Yougui, took the imperial seal, and gave it to the Last Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the western capital Yan joined Yuan Xiangxian; the palace guard killed Yougui, and Yan handed the imperial seal to the Last Emperor.

sentences.zh: 末帝立，巖自以有功於梁，又尚公主，聞唐駙馬杜悰位至將相，自奉甚豐，恥其不及。
